summary: Creates an IANA registry for the flags in the Prefix Information Option of IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Router Advertisements. Two flags were defined and six bits were left reserved, and another RFC had already used a flag without any registry existing. This document fixes that gap and updates RFC 4861.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8425 creates an IANA list for flags in the IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Prefix Information Option. It records the three currently defined flags and requires a Standards Action to add another.

subtitle: Creates an IANA registry for IPv6 Neighbor Discovery prefix flags.

tldr.problem: The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Prefix Information Option had flags defined in multiple RFCs but no IANA registry to track them.
tldr.mechanism: IANA creates a PIO flag registry, lists the L, A, and R flags, and requires Standards Action for new flags.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8425 updates RFC 4861 and says it has no security considerations.

today: RFC 8425 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 4861. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Prefix Information Option Flags
sections.content: The Prefix Information Option in an IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Router Advertisement has an eight-bit flag field. The L flag and A flag were defined in RFC 4861; RFC 6275 later defined the R flag without creating a registry or updating RFC 4861. RFC 8425 creates a registry for these PIO flags.
sections.plainLanguage: The flag field had definitions in more than one RFC, but no central registry. This document creates the registry and points RFC 4861 to it.

sections.title: The Registry and Assignment Rule
sections.content: The initial registry lists bit 0 as the L On-link flag, bit 1 as the A Autonomous Address Configuration flag, and bit 2 as the R Router Address flag. Bits 3 through 7 are reserved. Assigning new flags in the PIO header requires Standards Action.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry records the three defined flags and identifies bits 3 through 7 as reserved. A Standards Action is required to assign another flag.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 8425 states that it has no security considerations. It creates the registry and updates RFC 4861 to point to the registry as the place to find the current list of PIO flags.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC says it has no security considerations. It directs readers to the registry for the current flag list.
